finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: any visitor can make the server fetch an arbitrary URL via the 'feed' POST parameter. file_get_contents accepts http(s), ftp and file:// wrappers, so it can reach internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and local files. The response is not returned, but its byte length is echoed, which gives a size oracle and blind SSRF. Internal endpoints that act on a GET are also reachable.

trace.note: Branch entered for any POST with 'feed' set; require_admin() is not called
User value passed directly to file_get_contents, which fetches the URL or wrapper
strlen of fetched body echoed to the attacker (size oracle, enables probing of internal hosts, ports and files)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no DNS pinning, and redirects are followed by default. The only guard in the file, require_admin(), is defined at line 4 but is not applied to this branch. No framework or middleware exists in the directory. The set_webhook branch at line 17 also passes user input to curl_init, but it is gated by require_admin(), so it was not reported.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents and echoes strlen. require_admin() (defined at line 4) is only called in the set_webhook branch at line 18, and no allowlist or validation exists.
